content.text:
This is the commit that migrated the codebase from a previous iCal library (likely ical4j) to `biweekly` for ICS generation. This is clearly the origin of the bug: it introduced the `Biweekly.write(ical).go()` calls that never set a default timezone, causing the timezone-related bug fixed by 80dcd036.

Let me verify by checking whether the old code (before this commit) handled timezones explicitly, to confirm this migration is where the timezone-setting logic was lost.

content.text:
I've confirmed the flawed `Biweekly.write(ical).go()` line (which never sets a default timezone on the writer) was untouched between its introduction and the fix — it only appears/disappears in commits 93de21ca and 80dcd036, so the root cause traces cleanly to the earlier commit.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 93de21ca4af4279d8ac132e05a7692a7b75730f5

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** The fix commit (80dcd036) replaces four instances of the convenience call `Biweekly.write(ical).go(...)` with an explicit `ICalWriter` where `writer.getTimezoneInfo().setDefaultTimeZone(TimeZone.getDefault())` is called before writing. This strongly suggested the bug was a missing timezone configuration on the iCal writer. I used `git log -S"Biweekly.write"` on each of the four affected files to find when that exact string was added/removed. In all four files, the string was added in exactly one commit (93de21ca, "Thu Sep 4 2014") and removed only in the fix commit (80dcd036) — no intermediate commit touched the write call.

**(2) The introducing change:** Commit 93de21ca is a large migration commit that replaced the project's older, hand-rolled iCal generation (raw text output with `SimpleDateFormat` explicitly set to UTC, e.g. `df.setTimeZone(TimeZone.getTimeZone("UTC"))`) with the `biweekly` library (added as a new 3rd-party dependency in the same commit, per `pom.xml`/`.classpath`/`3rd_party` changes). In doing so, it set the timezone ID on individual `DateStart`/`DateEnd` properties (`setTimezoneId(TimeZone.getDefault().getID())`) but called `Biweekly.write(ical).go()`, the simple convenience writer, which never registers a default `VTIMEZONE` with the writer's `TimezoneInfo`. This means the generated ICS files referenced a timezone ID on date properties without ever emitting/registering an actual `VTIMEZONE` definition for it — causing calendar clients to potentially misinterpret local event times (the timezone bug fixed later).

**(3) Supporting evidence:** 
- Before 93de21ca, timestamps were manually formatted in UTC (verified via `git show 93de21ca^:...CalendarExport.java`), which was correct output.
- After 93de21ca, times are tagged with a local timezone ID via `setTimezoneId(...)` but the writer used (`Biweekly.write(...).go()`) has no mechanism invoked to declare that timezone, exactly the gap that 80dcd036 closes by switching to `ICalWriter` + `getTimezoneInfo().setDefaultTimeZone(...)`.
- All four files fixed in 80dcd036 were also the same four files modified in 93de21ca as part of the same library migration, and no other commit touched the vulnerable write calls in between.

I'm fairly confident in this attribution since the introduced and removed code lines match exactly and no intervening commits altered the relevant logic, but I did not build/run the code to empirically reproduce the timezone bug — this conclusion is based on code/history analysis only.
